messages:
alex: heads-up — canary shows a ~10% p99 bump after the token-lease change. throwing the small perf dump below, wondering if lease timing is interacting with batch formation/dispatch

maria: interesting. i saw a similar uptick on a svc test with long sequences. suspect lease window + batching cutoff causing more partial batches and fallback kernels

dan: can you paste the perf numbers / traces?

alex: pasted from canary run:
```
perf_summary: p50=28ms p95=112ms p99=418ms
requests=12k
avg_batch_size=3.2
lease_retries=218
kv_hit_rate=0.71
kernel_path: preferred=fused_attn_v2 fallback=generic_attn
note: many long-seq requests hitting fallback path around the same time window
```

jin: hmm. two hypotheses: 1) lease window aligns poorly with batch wait threshold -> more tiny batches and more kernel switches 2) admission policy allows bursts that exceed token budget and trigger fallback

sophie: we experimented with a hard token_budget_per_tick and it reduced fallback, but latency variance increased for small requests (they waited more). tradeoff was worse p50 but better p99 in that run

dan: i'd try a small-hysteresis on admission: only start shedding (soft-429) if queue_size > Q and sustained for T ms. also prefer kv-hit requests when admitting to preserve cheap wins

maria: agree. also consider lease-window scaling by seq distribution: shorter lease for <256 tokens, longer for >1024. that keeps short requests moving while letting long ones amortize batching

alex: prototype config i've been testing:
```json
{
  "admission": {
    "soft_429": {
      "enabled": true,
      "queue_threshold": 120,
      "sustained_ms": 250,
      "respect_kv_hits": true,
      "retry_after_seconds": 1
    },
    "lease_windows": [
      {"max_seq": 256, "window_ms": 12},
      {"max_seq": 1024, "window_ms": 24},
      {"max_seq": 65536, "window_ms": 40}
    ],
    "token_budget_per_tick": 1200
  }
}
```

jin: looks reasonable. also add a tiny randomized jitter to window boundaries so multiple requests don't align q-aligned batches

sophie: +1. and add a KV-priority admission bucket: if kv_hit -> admit even if slightly over budget, cap total kv-priority admitted per tick to avoid overload

dan: for rollout: canary with 5% traffic, collect kernel-switch rate, avg_batch_size, lease_retries, and p99. if kernel-switch rate drops and p99 improves -> promote

perf-bot: regression-check: flagged run 1895001228 as anomalous, created trace trace/rcv-1895-22. owners: @alex @dan

alex: action items:
- dan + jin: add hysteresis + jitter change to canary config (this afternoon)
- sophie: implement kv-priority cap and reporting metric (kv_admit_count)
- maria: prepare eval harness to replay long-seq workload and compare kernel-path counts
- i'll run canary and post results here in ~2 hours

dan: ack. will push small change, will include Prometheus counters: "admit.soft_429_count", "kv_admit_count", "kernel_fallback_count"

maria: if we still see fallback, fallback mitigation: schedule model-quantization variant for long-seq traffic as fallback route to reduce kernel mismatch cost

alex: thanks all. keeping this thread for the canary updates. :thumbsup:
